title: Grandfather indentured in Sicily and the family teaching gene
summary: His paternal grandfather taught the baron's children to read and was indentured; teaching runs in the family.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Well I know that the family history, some of it is in Joe’s book. You know Joe wrote a book on Bill Evans that’s coming out in September, his time with Bill Evans. And I heard you talk to Pat about education. And if there’s an education gene then we must have it because our paternal grandfather, excuse me, he was able to finish three grades of school before he got indentured to a baron. And it was really rough work and he died prematurely because of it. He would play with the baron’s children after church on Sunday because he wasn’t that much older, and he taught them how to read. I don’t know if he taught them how to write but he taught them how to read. And the baron was so knocked out because he was illiterate. Most of the nobility were illiterate and the church kind of ran their affairs for them, that he excused the indentured loan and gave my grandfather a piece of land to work on shares, to sharecrop. And then my father became a teacher, all three of us became teachers, my two sons are teachers. So there’s got to be some sort of gene there that’s, you know, passing that on. You have to really like it. You really have to love it and of course know what you’re teaching. Know the subject.
And that dated back to Sicily, that story you started?

Yeah. Yeah my grandfather, he was indentured, and again, my father, once he finally got that piece — you couldn’t own land in Sicily or Italy until Mussolini. Nobody could own land except the nobility. So once he was excused, see what happened, you know children are a commodity. There was no work for people. The children were a commodity. If you have a lot of children and the baron comes to you saying I need a worker, I’ll give you 500 lire and then you pay me back and you have your kid back. That’s the way it worked. And of course you never could find the 500 lire again, if you took it. And so and my grandfather only had one eye so he’s probably the most compromised of the family and so he was — and they probably figured this is a way for him to make a living or have a

life. But my father remembers when he was a little boy working out in the field with my grandfather. They had this piece of land and they would do the wheat and — so but the teaching was always there. I think it dates back at least to my grandfather. Yeah.
